correctness.rationale: Full dimension is (m−1)(n−1) because X_ij=a_i b_j/T is positive. The Hall positive-flow criterion after deleting at most two cells proves single facet condition a_i+b_j<T and the pairwise same-row/same-column/disjoint conditions. Without strict support an extra coordinate is forced zero; connectedness of K_{m,n} after deleting at most three cells except impossible isolated-margin cases gives codimension at least three. The Frobenius tangent projector is P_m Z P_n, with pair-normal cosine -1/(n−1), -1/(m−1), +1/((m−1)(n−1)). The central inequalities 1/m+2/n<1 and 2/m+1/n<1 fail only for 3x3. In the mean-angle formula A=m−1,B=n−1, AB asin(1/AB)−A asin(1/A)−B asin(1/B) -> -1, whereas the disjoint-class scaled angle approaches +1. Independently solved 1,440 strict positive common-slack LPs across dimensions 3x3–4x4 and checked all predicted facet pairs; finite LPs corroborate only, the Hall/projector proof supplies universal and equality cases.
residual_risks: The LP uses numerical margins and a positive slack tolerance; exact wall equality is established symbolically, not numerically.
The two acute angle types coincide numerically when m=n; they remain separately labeled incidence types.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general support-graph max-flow theorem provides the feasibility tool; a published intrinsic inradius/center formula addresses distances to coordinate facets, not intersection normal products, all pairwise strict triple-margin walls, or angular sampling.

value.rationale: The exact pairwise margin walls characterize a natural face-adjacency invariant without generic margins, including sharp equality boundaries and the central 3x3 exception. The metric normal-product classification makes a mathematically motivated distinction between a typical asymptotically obtuse scaled angle (+1) and a negative scaled mean (−1), a rare-event phenomenon meaningful beyond a routine Hall restatement.
residual_risks: No extension claimed for 2-row/2-column cases or structural zero constraints.
